newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - March 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - March 11.

text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Tuesday, as reported by Kyodo news agency.
-- Prosecutors say Takeshi Abe, once the country's top authority on haemophilia, received 100 million yen from drug makers.
-- Three firms affiliated with Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd will be merged into investment advising company.
-- Poll shows support rate for Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto cabinet drops to 36.1 percent.
-- Prosecutors say Takeshi Abe had strong influence in determining haemophilia treatment in Japan.
-- Government plans to present bills to parliament to revise Bank of Japan and anti-monopoly laws.
-- Japan Federation of Economic Organizations (Keidanren) may suspend membership of Nomura Securities Co Ltd for its suspicious stock dealings.
